editorNote: Today's mix: a 125B model squeezed onto gaming hardware, a Danish population-register breach that began with a legitimate company's access, and agent plumbing from Cloudflare. A robotics unicorn and a Huawei–Qualcomm patent truce fill out the business side.

stories.headline: Denmark discloses unauthorized access to 8.8 million people's CPR records
stories.summary: Danish authorities said a private company's legitimate access to the Central Person Register was misused during September, exposing names, addresses and ID numbers for about 8.8 million records, including deceased people and those who have moved abroad. The administrators spotted irregular activity on Oct. 2, revoked the company's access and notified the data protection authority.
stories.whyItMatters: A legitimate third-party access channel, not a break-in, was the weak point, and the register holds roughly 11 million records overall.

stories.headline: Strata runs a 125B Qwen model on a single consumer GPU
stories.summary: The open-source Strata engine runs Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) on gaming PCs with 12 GB+ VRAM and 32 GB+ RAM by spreading weights across GPU, system RAM and SSD. Its README reports 53 tokens/s output on an RTX 5070, plus a 1.6–1.8x speedup from speculative decoding.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how far memory tiering can push local inference, though the README notes 1–3 minute load freezes and one-request-at-a-time serving by default.

stories.headline: Cloudflare launches a beta Web Search API for agents
stories.summary: The API lets agents and apps search the web through REST or a Workers AI binding, routed via AI Gateway with logging and Zero Data Retention support. Ceramic.ai, Exa and Linkup are the launch providers, billed at their standard rates with no Cloudflare markup.
stories.whyItMatters: Cloudflare now bundles search grounding into the same billing and logging path as its AI Gateway traffic.

stories.headline: Huawei and Qualcomm sign a multi-year patent cross-license
stories.summary: The October 5 announcement covers reciprocal licenses across 5G, compute, AI and networking, plus Qualcomm's acquisition of select Huawei U.S. patents. Both sides cite FRAND principles, and the transaction needs regulatory approval before closing.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a formal licensing arrangement between the two companies, still contingent on regulators.

sourceLinks.title: Huawei and Qualcomm Announce Broad Patent License Agreement - Huawei

stories.headline: Germany's RobCo passes a $1 billion valuation in an employee share sale
stories.summary: The Munich robotics company crossed $1 billion through a secondary sale, doubling its valuation in nine months, with Sequoia, Lightspeed and others plus new investors Cherry Ventures and European Tech Collective. It follows a $100 million Series C in January 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: The valuation came via a secondary rather than new primary capital.

sourceLinks.title: Europe's new robotics unicorn: Germany's RobCo hits $1B valuation - Tech Funding News
